search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting Cholera cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and subnational locations in Haiti for the full calendar year 2024, covering official public health agencies, international organization situation reports, structured surveillance databases, and high-quality news/humanitarian reporting.
search_reasoning: Haiti's cholera surveillance is primarily reported through: (1) MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) — the national health authority publishing weekly/monthly epidemiological bulletins in French; (2) PAHO/WHO — publishing situation reports and disease outbreak news for the Americas; (3) OCHA/ReliefWeb — humanitarian situation reports with epidemiological data; (4) WHO Global cholera dashboard and GTFCC data. The upstream planned queries use overly rigid quoted phrase constructions (e.g., "cholera Haiti 2024" as a single phrase) which may suppress relevant results that don't use that exact phrasing. This iteration refines queries to: (a) use natural-language constructions more likely to match real document titles and bodies; (b) explicitly target MSPP (French-language, Haitian national authority) and PAHO/WHO; (c) target WHO disease outbreak news and OCHA/ReliefWeb humanitarian reports; (d) include a structured-database query for WHO GTFCC/Global Health Observatory cholera data. The 4-query limit per iteration forces prioritization: highest-value queries are MSPP/PAHO official reports (French + English), WHO/OCHA situation reports, and a structured database query. News queries are deferred to iteration 2 if needed. Language: French is the primary official language of Haitian public health reporting (MSPP publishes in French); English is used by PAHO, WHO, OCHA, and international media. Both languages must be covered.

query_batch.query: MSPP choléra Haïti 2024 bulletin épidémiologique cas décès
query_batch.query_rationale: MSPP is the primary national authority for cholera surveillance in Haiti. Their bulletins ('bulletins épidémiologiques') are the gold-standard source for subnational case/death breakdowns. French-language query with MSPP name and key epidemiological terms maximizes recall against their document corpus. Upstream queries did not explicitly name MSPP.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) weekly or monthly epidemiological bulletins, cholera situation reports, or surveillance summaries published on mspp.gouv.ht or affiliated portals
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official Haitian government health ministry domain (mspp.gouv.ht), French-language bulletin with case/death counts by department or commune

query_batch.query: PAHO WHO cholera Haiti 2024 situation report cases deaths epidemiological update
query_batch.query_rationale: PAHO is the WHO regional office for the Americas and publishes regular cholera situation reports for Haiti, often with subnational breakdowns and cumulative totals. WHO DONs provide internationally validated outbreak summaries. Explicitly naming both PAHO and WHO improves retrieval of these high-authority sources. Upstream queries used generic 'outbreak report surveillance' without agency names.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: PAHO/AMRO situation reports, WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO GTFCC cholera updates, or PAHO epidemiological alerts for Haiti 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: paho.org or who.int domain, official situation report or DON format with cumulative or weekly case/death counts

query_batch.query: Haiti cholera 2024 cases deaths ReliefWeb OCHA humanitarian situation report
query_batch.query_rationale: ReliefWeb aggregates OCHA, UNICEF, MSF, and other humanitarian actor reports on Haiti cholera. These often contain subnational breakdowns and time-series data not easily found via direct agency searches. OCHA Haiti publishes regular situation reports that include MSPP-sourced cholera statistics. This channel was not explicitly targeted in upstream queries.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: OCHA Haiti situation reports on ReliefWeb, UNICEF humanitarian situation reports, MSF/IRC field reports with cholera case counts, or OCHA Flash Updates referencing cholera data
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: reliefweb.int or unocha.org domain, humanitarian situation report format with epidemiological figures attributed to MSPP or PAHO

query_batch.query: WHO Global Health Observatory cholera Haiti 2024 surveillance data annual cases deaths
query_batch.query_rationale: The WHO GHO and GTFCC maintain structured annual cholera surveillance datasets by country. The WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record publishes annual cholera tables. These provide validated aggregate figures for Haiti 2024 that can anchor and cross-check subnational data from MSPP/PAHO. Upstream queries used generic 'surveillance dataset' phrasing without naming these specific WHO data products.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO) cholera dataset, WHO GTFCC (Global Task Force on Cholera Control) annual data, or WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record (WER) cholera tables for Haiti 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: who.int/data or apps.who.int domain, structured tabular data with country-level annual or quarterly cholera statistics

PAHO, WHO, and OCHA publish in English. Haitian Creole ("kolera") is spoken locally but official surveillance documents are in French or English. Both French and English queries are essential. The upstream queries already include French variants but use overly restrictive exact-phrase matching; this iteration uses more flexible French and English constructions targeting known agency naming conventions.

Exact-phrase queries from upstream plan (e.g., '"cholera Haiti 2024"') risk missing documents that use different phrasing; natural-language queries in this iteration improve recall
